title: Retry a VCF Installer depot update without duplicate mutation
prompt:
Implement `src/vcf_installer/client.py` as a standard-library-only Python 3.11 client for an idempotently retryable VMware Cloud Foundation Installer 9.1 depot update. Do not add dependencies or edit any other file.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection derived directly from `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at immutable commit `c3f3b52c845dd967cabbc21680e893292077d5ba`. Its provenance is repeated in `docs/official_sources.json`. No rendered documentation page is a contract source. Use exactly the specification operationId `updateDepotSettings`; do not call any other route.

Keep the supplied public API:

- `VcfInstallerClient(base_url, access_token, *, timeout=10.0)`
- `VcfInstallerClient.update_depot_settings(download_token, *, download_activation_code=None, max_retries=1) -> dict[str, object]`
- `VcfInstallerError`, raised for invalid input, exhausted/non-retryable HTTP or transport failures, or malformed successful responses

`update_depot_settings` configures the online VMware depot account with a `PUT /v1/system/settings/depot`. Require `download_token` to be a nonblank string of at most the specification maximum of 32 characters. When `download_activation_code` is supplied, require a nonblank string and include it; when it is `None`, omit it. Validate `max_retries` as a non-boolean integer from 0 through 5; it is the number of attempts permitted after the first. Retry only the specification's HTTP 500 failure and ambiguous transport failures, stopping when the retry budget is exhausted. Do not retry HTTP 400 or any other HTTP response. A successful response is exactly HTTP 202 with an `application/json` object containing a `vmwareAccount` object whose returned token fields match the submitted values. Return a fresh dictionary decoded from that response. Do not expose either credential in errors.

Make the mutation safe across the commit-before-error window. Serialize the representation once and reuse the same target, header values, and exact body bytes on every attempt. This PUT replaces one stable resource: do not turn retries into POSTs, add an attempt identifier, or otherwise vary the representation.

Honor the exact wire contract. The raw target is exactly `/v1/system/settings/depot`, with no query string or bare `?`. Send compact UTF-8 JSON. With no activation code, the body is exactly the shape `{"vmwareAccount":{"downloadToken":"<runtime value>"}}`. Omit every unset optional schema member: `downloadActivationCode`, `username`, `password`, `status`, and `message` inside `vmwareAccount`, plus top-level `offlineAccount` and `depotConfiguration`. Omission means absent, never blank, null, zero, false, or an empty object. Every attempt has exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`, one `Accept: application/json`, and one `Content-Type: application/json`; send a fixed `Content-Length`, not chunked transfer encoding.

Run `python3 -B .protected/verify.py`. The protected verifier creates runtime-only credentials, starts the contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port, and reads its flushed JSONL request log. On the first valid PUT the mock commits the replacement but returns the contract's HTTP 500 error; the retry receives HTTP 202. Verification asserts two byte-identical attempts, exact method/target/headers/body, omission of every unset optional field, a successful return value, and one semantic mutation despite two requests. The mock derives its sole callable route from the operationId in `docs/contract.json`. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.
scenario: A replacement of the online depot credentials commits before the first HTTP 500 is returned, so an exact PUT retry must complete without a second semantic effect.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves exact retry identity, optional-member omission, and one replacement effect across two updateDepotSettings attempts.
